title: Average-case hardness of multiplicatively approximating Gaussian permanents
formal: Is multiplicative approximation of the permanent of an independent complex Gaussian matrix, on a sufficiently large fraction of instances, #P-hard under randomized polynomial-time reductions as in the Permanent-of-Gaussians Conjecture?
definitions: For X∈ℂ^(n×n), Per(X)=Σ_{σ∈S_n}∏_i X_(i,σ(i)). The entries are independent standard complex Gaussians. The GPE× task receives accuracy and failure parameters ε,δ and should return z with |z−Per(X)|≤ε|Per(X)| on at least a 1−δ fraction of matrices. This concerns the complex permanent itself; hardness of worst-case permanent evaluation or additive approximation alone does not give this claim.

context_blocks.text: Boson-sampling probabilities are governed by matrix permanents. Average-case hardness addresses whether the apparent difficulty persists on the random matrices relevant to that model.

Aaronson and Arkhipov state the Permanent-of-Gaussians Conjecture separately from their anti-concentration conjecture. The distinction matters: neither the worst-case #P-completeness of the permanent nor an assumption about tiny probabilities establishes the average-case reduction.

why: Establish a major complexity foundation for a restricted quantum sampling model.
answer_criterion: Prove the stated proposition or its logical negation, with the specified quantifiers, model and guarantees. A conditional theorem settles only that conditional claim. Benchmark acceptance requires a complete proof-assistant-checked proof of the full target.
